question: What is the primary goal of the staffing function in healthcare management?

options.A: Providing adequate personnel for safe patient care
options.B: Minimizing the promotion of senior nursing officers
options.C: Increasing the number of administrative meetings daily
options.D: Reducing the total operational budget of the hospital

explanation: Staffing focuses primarily on ensuring enough qualified staff are present to deliver safe and effective care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h1)

question: How does proper staffing directly influence clinical outcomes in a hospital?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any ongoing staff training
options.B: It stops patients from getting admitted on weekends
options.C: It guarantees automatic salary increases for all workers
options.D: It lowers the frequency of adverse patient safety events

explanation: Adequate nurse staffing reduces errors and improves overall patient safety and recovery rates. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h1)

question: What factor is most critical when calculating patient acuity for staffing?

options.A: The marital status of the admitted patient
options.B: The brand of medication prescribed by the doctor
options.C: The severity of illness and care complexity
options.D: The distance of the patient from the nurses' station

explanation: Acuity systems evaluate how sick a patient is and how much nursing care they require. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why do nurse managers monitor staff turnover rates during workforce planning?

options.A: To calculate the exact electricity consumption of wards
options.B: To predict future vacancies and plan recruitment drives
options.C: To reduce the number of visiting doctors in the hospital
options.D: To decide which nurses deserve a formal warning query

explanation: Tracking turnover helps managers anticipate when positions will become vacant so replacements can be planned. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h2)

question: What document must every registered nurse present during employment screening in Nigeria?

options.A: A personal letter of recommendation from a politician
options.B: Receipt for hospital car park access
options.C: Proof of membership in a social club
options.D: Current practicing license from the NMCN

explanation: A valid license from the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is mandatory for legal practice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the main difference between recruitment and selection in staffing?

options.A: Recruitment only applies to auxiliary staff members
options.B: Selection happens before job advertising takes place
options.C: Recruitment attracts applicants, while selection chooses the best candidate
options.D: Recruitment is done by doctors, while selection is done by patients

explanation: Recruitment builds a pool of applicants, whereas selection narrows that pool down to hire the right person. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the primary role of a preceptor during a new nurse's orientation?

options.A: Handling the administrative payroll and tax deductions
options.B: Deciding when the hospital canteen should open
options.C: Evaluating the hospital building maintenance schedules
options.D: Providing guidance, supervision, and clinical mentorship

explanation: A preceptor supports and guides the new staff member through daily clinical duties. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why is structured unit-specific orientation important for newly employed nurses?

options.A: It helps them learn specialized ward routines and equipment quickly
options.B: It replaces the need for an initial nursing qualification
options.C: It allows them to bypass hospital safety regulations
options.D: It ensures they never have to work night shifts

explanation: Different wards have unique equipment and protocols that new staff must learn to practice safely. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is a major challenge affecting nurse-patient ratios in many Nigerian public hospitals?

options.A: Excessive number of nurses reporting for every single shift
options.B: Shortage of qualified nursing personnel relative to patient load
options.C: Ban on working night shifts by the health ministry
options.D: Mandatory limit of two patients per ward per day

explanation: Brain drain and funding gaps often result in high patient-to-nurse ratios across public facilities. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why is maintaining a proper skill mix on every shift important?

options.A: It guarantees that all patients are discharged by midday
options.B: It prevents nurses from taking their mandatory annual leave
options.C: It ensures junior staff have experienced support for complex tasks
options.D: It eliminates the need for any shift handovers

explanation: A balanced skill mix ensures less experienced nurses can consult senior colleagues when managing unstable patients. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting regular performance appraisals for nurses?

options.A: Providing constructive feedback and identifying areas for growth
options.B: Reducing the number of patients admitted to the ward
options.C: Determining the exact cost of hospital medical supplies
options.D: Finding reasons to dismiss senior staff members immediately

explanation: Appraisals help evaluate work quality, offer feedback, and support professional development. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h6)

question: How do direct observation competency assessments improve patient safety?

options.A: They replace the need for professional nursing registration
options.B: They ensure nurses finish their duties before schedule
options.C: They verify that clinical procedures are performed correctly and safely
options.D: They prevent patients from complaining about food quality

explanation: Watching a nurse perform procedures confirms they follow established safety protocols. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h6)

question: What term describes educational sessions conducted within the hospital for working staff?
explanation: In-service training refers to ongoing educational programs provided right inside the healthcare facility. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h7)

question: Why are staff development and retention strategies linked together in hospital management?

options.A: Retention makes professional nursing exams completely optional
options.B: Staff development stops nurses from ever taking sick leave
options.C: Nurses tend to stay longer when they see opportunities for career growth
options.D: Training programs automatically increase the hospital electricity bill

explanation: Investing in staff education boosts morale and encourages nurses to remain with the institution. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h7)

question: What major staffing challenge involves skilled nurses leaving the country for better opportunities abroad?
explanation: Brain drain refers to the emigration of trained professionals seeking better working conditions elsewhere. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h8)

question: What is a major ethical concern when a ward is severely understaffed?

options.A: Automatic promotion for all junior nurses on duty
options.B: Elimination of all documentation requirements in the hospital
options.C: Compromised patient safety and risk of professional negligence
options.D: Reduction in the cost of hospital drugs for patients

explanation: Severe staff shortages stretch nurses thin, increasing the risk of errors and ethical breaches in care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h8)
